# Original calibration estimator observations

These files are original-only observations from [Actions run 39539792161](https://github.com/bin9208/openpilot-rust/actions/runs/39539792161), job 119024670326, artifact 12319335594. The diagnostic workflow head was `adac9d8a363aab6057b5ba3477c2ca89f7646847`; its pinned checkout was `5bcfae4482d9c4dcb1da46e1086bea609e0c9688`. The original-only driver SHA256 was `08e7811d5760dfec98a707532da3c35e7beeac24306a82d71840d96b582ea96b`. It called `histories()` and loaded the original `calibrationd.py` class through `calibration_reference.original()`. No Rust candidate ran during capture.

The public artifact ZIP SHA256 is `a872706ecacea6bfec2d18f944b0f06a79d8d2e51da7aa36bb7c916b3d970a5c`. `manifest.json` SHA256 is `a8144a49c71ffae8c46b595d0fde684b71784f2574149bb81fb65c62c0dde663`; `original.jsonl.gz` SHA256 is `9ea4da7d3216e19a2fcaf4043c928d59f7b4014e2aa7f6ee2b4c401b3f045de8`. It contains 15,128 ordered requests, 15,098 full state/packet observations, 30 source errors, and 14 saved Params packet writes. There were 163 reset attempts: 147 successful observations and 16 source errors. A handler scoped to each original constructor observed one cached-Params exception among those successful resets. The manifest pins all original code/schema sources and package versions. The compressed file is retained byte-for-byte from the artifact; it is independent expected data, not a native-produced reference.

This replaces the first original-only capture from [run 39537326538](https://github.com/bin9208/openpilot-rust/actions/runs/39537326538), job 119016882232, artifact 12317567332, captured at checkout `04ee2c46963a27cbc9d37cea524f169a63557913`. Its trace SHA256 was `2404a796dc09886770546197417d325d53aa2f1d451722982bf7f319439ce954`. The delta capture compared all 15,128 rows against that independently sealed trace and required exact equality after removing only the new `saved_error` boolean from each successful reset row. An independent data audit repeated this comparison: 146 `false`, one `true`, and no other changed row or source hash. The old capture remains available through its artifact; it is not duplicated in the repository.

The Rust test sends those exact requests to a freshly built `calibration_trace` ELF. It compares every state and complete decoded Event with the historical `2e-12` Float64 policy and one adjacent Float32 value (with the original `2e-12` cancellation floor) for packet float lists. Discrete fields, packet structure, validity, timestamp, accepted position, error position, cached-Params failure observation, and persistence position are exact. Captured saved packet contents are compared against the native publication packet after applying the original saved Event header (`logMonoTime=0`, `valid=true`). This verifies the contents proposed for persistence; `calibration_trace` exposes a persistence flag rather than performing a Params write. The test is a host estimator comparison, not a device or daemon lifecycle acceptance result.
